models.notes: Used for the Phase-0 go/no-go latency spike (T-0.10/T-0.11) and later as the resident face detector (F-C04). Fetched via scripts/fetch-models.ts, never bundled unverified. [Fixed in Phase 4, T-4.4] inputShape was recorded as [1,3,160,120] from an unverified assumption; real inference against the model shows a fixed [1,3,640,640] input (ORT rejects any other spatial size) with a 3-stride (8/16/32) anchor-free YOLOX-style head (cls/obj/bbox/kps outputs per stride), matching opencv_zoo's face_detection_yunet_2023mar. See `src/perception/models/face.ts`.

architecture.md §6.3's PP-OCRv5 mobile detector (T-6.3). Real ORT introspection (2026-09-18): input `x` is [N,3,H,W] with H/W dynamic (a DB/DBNet-style segmentation detector, NOT an anchor decoder like YuNet — design.md §6.4's 'detector on unexplained regions, long side ≤ 960px' controls the resize before inference, padded to a multiple of 32 as DBNet requires). Output `fetch_name_0` is a single-channel probability map at the same spatial resolution as the (possibly downsampled) input; text boxes come from thresholding + contour-finding + the DB unclip formula, not a direct box regression head. See `src/perception/models/ocr-det.ts`.

architecture.md §6.3's Latin/English recognizer — smaller than the multilingual `ch_` variant, matching the doc's own 'measure' note (7.9MB here vs. the ~16MB multilingual figure architecture.md cites). Real ORT introspection (2026-09-18): output is [N, T, 438] (T dynamic) — a per-timestep class distribution over PaddleOCR's CTC vocabulary, verified exactly (see below). Input `x`'s ORT-reported shape is [N(dynamic), 3, '?', W(dynamic)] — the height dimension's own metadata is an unlabelled '?', not a number; height=48 (design.md §6.4's cited figure) was instead confirmed the way that matters more than metadata — a real successful end-to-end inference run: `test/browser/ocr-pipeline.spec.ts` renders the literal text 'HELLO WORLD' via a real `<canvas>` 2D context, runs it through the real bundled detector AND this recognizer at height=48, and gets back an EXACT decode match. Vocabulary size verified against PaddleOCR's own `rec_postprocess.py` (`CTCLabelDecode.add_special_char`: `['blank'] + dict_character`, where `dict_character` already has a trailing space appended when `use_space_char=True`): index 0 = CTC blank, indices 1-436 = `ocr_rec_ppocrv5_mobile_en.dict.txt`'s 436 lines in order, index 437 = space. 1+436+1=438, matching the real output dimension exactly — not assumed.

design.md §6.4's script-routing recognizer: 'if the line's character set detection or page lang suggests Devanagari, use the Devanagari recognizer when bundled.' Real ORT introspection (2026-09-18): output is [N, T, 570], confirmed by an actual inference-session load, not inferred by pattern-matching from the English model. Vocabulary: index 0 = CTC blank, indices 1-568 = `ocr_rec_ppocrv5_mobile_devanagari.dict.txt`'s 568 lines in order, index 569 = space. 1+568+1=570, matching exactly. Height=48 (design.md §6.4's cited figure) confirmed correct by a real successful end-to-end inference run, not just metadata: `test/browser/ocr-pipeline.spec.ts` renders the real word 'आधार' (Aadhaar) via a real `<canvas>` 2D context and gets back an EXACT decode match at 99.9% confidence through the full detect→crop→recognize pipeline — the strongest verification this project's OCR work has, since (unlike face photographs) there is no licensing barrier to rendering real, known ground-truth text.

436 lines, one character per line, UTF-8. Paired with `ocr-rec-ppocrv5-mobile-en` via that entry's `dict` field. sha256 computed and pinned here directly (no published hash found for this specific file upstream, unlike the .onnx models) — verify against a fresh download if this file is ever suspected corrupted.

568 lines, one character per line, UTF-8. Paired with `ocr-rec-ppocrv5-mobile-devanagari` via that entry's `dict` field. sha256 computed and pinned here directly (no published hash found for this specific file upstream).

models.notes: Real ORT introspection + accuracy check (2026-09-25): exported via torch.onnx.export from open_clip's ViT-B-32-quickgelu/openai vision tower, wrapped to L2-normalize its own output so the browser never needs to. int8-quantized (fp32 source was 351,604,555 bytes; this is dynamic-range INT8, ~4x smaller). Verified against the unquantized fp32 export on a real generated QR-code image and a plain-color control: both models classify the QR code top-1 'QR code' (softmax 0.197 fp32 vs 0.199 int8) and the plain image top-1 'plain background' (0.132 vs 0.121) — no observed accuracy loss from quantization. [A] no fixed download URL exists for this artifact (it is generated, not fetched from a stable third-party host) — `scripts/fetch-models.ts` only verifies the sha256 of what's already on disk here; regenerating from scratch on a fresh checkout requires re-running both export scripts with network access to Hugging Face Hub (open_clip's own weight download), not `fetch-models.ts` alone. See docs/HISTORY.md's 2026-09-25 T-4.5/T-4.6 entry.
